title: Humour, irony and wordplay
summary: How Spanish speakers joke: irony markers like ¡Lo que faltaba! and menudo + noun, mocking diminutives, understatement and hyperbole, puns built on polysemy, and the words for talking about humour.
focus: Recognising and using irony, understatement, mocking diminutives and puns
content:
## Irony markers

Spanish irony often uses a set exclamation, and tone does the rest.

| marker | ironic use |
|---|---|
| **¡Hombre, claro!** | "oh, sure" when the answer is plainly no |
| **¡Qué bien!** | something has just gone wrong |
| **menudo/a + noun** | what a…! **¡Menudo día!** (agrees: **¡Menuda tarde!**) |
| **vaya + noun** | **¡Vaya nochecita!** what a night (not a good one) |
| **¡Lo que faltaba!** | that's all we needed |
| **¡Anda que…!** | a reproach: **¡Anda que avisas!** you might have warned me |

Before the noun, **menudo** means "what a"; after it, plain "small" (**un hombre menudo**). Both can also admire: **¡Menudo gol!**

## Diminutives and augmentatives with a sting

Diminutives usually sound fond, but aimed at someone's cleverness they mock:

- **el listillo / la listilla**: the smart aleck who always knows better.
- **el cerebrito**: the brainiac, teasing but mostly friendly (**Clara es un cerebrito**).
- **el graciosillo**: someone trying too hard to be funny.
- **el muy + adjective** sharpens it: **Se fue sin pagar, el muy listillo.**

On a disaster, a diminutive shrinks it ironically: a flooded kitchen is **un problemilla**. Augmentatives cut both ways: **un cochazo** (a flash car, admiring), **un problemón** (a huge problem).

## Understatement and hyperbole

**Understatement** says less than the truth and lets the listener add the rest:

- **No está nada mal.** It's excellent (said of a record-breaking time).
- **Es un pelín caro.** It costs a fortune.
- **Hace un poquito de calor.** At forty-four degrees in the shade.

**Hyperbole** says far more:

- **Te lo he dicho mil veces.** I've told you a thousand times.
- **Me muero de hambre.** I'm starving.
- **Tardó un siglo en contestar.** He took ages to answer.

Both turn ironic when the gap with reality is the joke. Deadpan understatement is the heart of **la retranca**, the sly humour often associated with Galicia.

## Puns from polysemy

A **juego de palabras** needs one word with two live meanings:

| word | meaning 1 | meaning 2 |
|---|---|---|
| **el banco** | bank | bench |
| **la cola** | queue | glue (also tail) |
| **el gato** | cat | car jack |
| **la sierra** | saw | mountain range |

- **El banco del parque no da intereses, pero te deja sentarte.** The park bench pays no interest, but lets you sit.
- **Había tanta cola en la papelería que me quedé pegado.** So much queue (glue) at the stationer's that I got stuck.
- **El carpintero veranea en la sierra: no sabe desconectar.** The carpenter holidays in the mountains (the saw): he can't switch off.

## Talking about humour

- **tomar el pelo a alguien**: to pull someone's leg. **¿Me estás tomando el pelo?**
- **con segundas**: with a hidden meaning or a dig. **Lo dijo con segundas.**
- **pillar el chiste**: to get the joke (colloquial; **no lo pillo**).
- **el humor negro**: dark humour about death or misfortune; know your audience.
- **la retranca**: dry, deadpan irony.

**Irony vs sarcasm.** **La ironía** says the opposite of what it means and invites you to share the wink. **El sarcasmo** is irony sharpened to wound. **¡Qué puntual!** to a friend who turns up late is irony; repeated in front of the whole office to embarrass them, it is sarcasm.

vocabulary.meaning: what a…! (before a noun; ironic or admiring; agrees: menuda, menudos)
vocabulary.example: ¡Menudo atasco a las ocho de la mañana!
vocabulary.example_meaning: What a traffic jam at eight in the morning!

vocabulary.meaning: well, of course! (often ironic: of course not)
vocabulary.example: ¿Que si quiero hacer horas extra el domingo? ¡Hombre, claro!
vocabulary.example_meaning: Do I want to work overtime on Sunday? Oh, sure!

vocabulary.example: Se ha ido la luz en mitad de la cena. ¡Lo que faltaba!
vocabulary.example_meaning: The power's gone off in the middle of dinner. That's all we needed!

vocabulary.meaning: ironic reproach: ¡anda que avisas! = you might have warned me
vocabulary.example: ¡Anda que me llamas el día de mi cumpleaños!
vocabulary.example_meaning: You didn't even call me on my birthday!

vocabulary.example: El listillo de turno ya ha encontrado un fallo en el plan.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The resident smart aleck has already found a flaw in the plan.

vocabulary.example: Pregúntale a Clara, que es el cerebrito de la oficina.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Ask Clara, she's the office brainiac.

vocabulary.example: Tu paella no está nada mal: voy a repetir.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Your paella isn't bad at all: I'm having seconds.

vocabulary.example: ¿Te han ascendido otra vez? Me estás tomando el pelo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Promoted again? You're pulling my leg.

vocabulary.meaning: with a hidden meaning or a dig
vocabulary.example: Cuando me felicitó por mi puntualidad, lo dijo con segundas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: When she congratulated me on my punctuality, there was a dig in it.

vocabulary.example: Tardé un rato en pillar el chiste, pero luego me reí más que nadie.
vocabulary.example_meaning: It took me a while to get the joke, but then I laughed more than anyone.

vocabulary.example: El humor negro funciona entre amigos, no con desconocidos.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Dark humour works among friends, not with strangers.

vocabulary.example: Con mucha retranca, mi tío llamó llovizna al diluvio.
vocabulary.example_meaning: With a perfectly straight face, my uncle called the downpour a drizzle.

vocabulary.example: El juego de palabras se pierde en la traducción.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The pun gets lost in translation.

vocabulary.example: Su sarcasmo en la reunión dejó a todos incómodos.
vocabulary.example_meaning: His sarcasm in the meeting made everyone uncomfortable.

quiz.prompt: It's raining, you've just missed the bus, and now your umbrella turns inside out. What do you say?
quiz.explanation: ¡Lo que faltaba! (that's all we needed) greets the last straw. ¡Menos mal! means 'thank goodness', which only works if something went right.

quiz.prompt: ¡___ nochecita he pasado con el vecino de la batería! (menudo)
quiz.explanation: Menudo before a noun means 'what a…!' and agrees with it, so la nochecita takes ¡Menuda nochecita!

quiz.prompt: Your boss asks if you'd love to work this Saturday. You reply, flatly: '¡Hombre, claro! Me hace muchísima ilusión.' What do you mean?
quiz.explanation: Said flat, ¡Hombre, claro! and the over-the-top 'muchísima ilusión' mean the opposite: irony through tone.
hints: Listen to the tone, not the words.

quiz.prompt: Llevas un mes en la ciudad y ni un mensaje. ¡___ que me llamas!
quiz.explanation: ¡Anda que…! + a verb in the present is an ironic reproach: ¡Anda que me llamas! = you haven't called me once.

quiz.prompt: Which word teases a studious, very bright person, usually fondly?
quiz.explanation: El cerebrito (little brain) is teasing but friendly. El listillo mocks a know-it-all; el cabezota is a stubborn person.
hints: Think of the brain: el cerebro.

quiz.prompt: Se coló en la cola y encima sonrió, el muy ___. (listo + -illo)
quiz.explanation: El muy + an ironic diminutive is a mocking aside: el muy listillo = the clever so-and-so.

quiz.prompt: —He ganado el maratón y he batido el récord. —Pues no está nada ___.
quiz.explanation: No está nada mal (it's not bad at all) is understatement. The speaker means it is excellent.

quiz.prompt: Tranquilo, no es verdad: te estaba tomando el ___.
quiz.explanation: Tomar el pelo a alguien (literally to take someone's hair) is to pull their leg.

quiz.prompt: 'Había tanta cola en la papelería que me quedé pegado.' The joke works because cola means both…
quiz.explanation: The long queue at the stationer's and the glue sold there are both cola, and 'me quedé pegado' (I got stuck) brings the glue to life.

quiz.prompt: As a downpour floods the street, your neighbour remarks with a straight face: 'Parece que chispea un poco.' What kind of humour is this?
quiz.explanation: Chispear is to drizzle. Calling a flood a drizzle, deadpan, is the dry understatement of la retranca. There is no pun and nothing dark about it.

conversations.title: The humour column
conversations.scenario: Inés, an editor at a weekly magazine, goes through Bruno's humour column with him before it goes to print.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: He leído tu columna. Menuda forma de empezar, con un juego de palabras.
lines.meaning: I've read your column. Some way to start, with a pun.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¿No te gusta? El banco del parque no da intereses, pero te deja sentarte. Es bueno.
lines.meaning: Don't you like it? The park bench pays no interest, but it lets you sit. It's good.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Hombre, claro, buenísimo. He tenido que leerlo tres veces para pillar el chiste.
lines.meaning: Oh, sure, brilliant. I had to read it three times to get the joke.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Un poquito. Pero el del carpintero que se va de vacaciones a la sierra sí funciona.
lines.meaning: A little. But the one about the carpenter who goes to the mountains on holiday does work.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Porque no sabe desconectar. Me costó una semana dar con él.
lines.meaning: Because he can't switch off. It took me a week to come up with it.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Lo que me preocupa es el párrafo del alcalde. Ahí ya no hay ironía: hay sarcasmo.
lines.meaning: What worries me is the paragraph about the mayor. That's not irony any more: it's sarcasm.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¿Tú crees? Solo digo que es muy puntual para llegar tarde.
lines.meaning: Do you think so? I only say he's very punctual about arriving late.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: La ironía guiña el ojo; el sarcasmo muerde. Y ese párrafo muerde.
lines.meaning: Irony winks; sarcasm bites. And that paragraph bites.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Vale, lo suavizo. ¿Algo más, señora editora?
lines.meaning: All right, I'll tone it down. Anything else, madam editor?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Sí: no vuelvas a llamarme cerebrito en la reunión de redacción.
lines.meaning: Yes: don't call me a brainiac in the editorial meeting again.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¡Anda que no te gustó! Te pusiste roja como un tomate.
lines.meaning: Oh, come on, you loved it! You went as red as a tomato.

guide.tip: Irony sits in the tone. Say ¡Qué bien! flat and slow, eyes on the disaster, and nobody will take it literally.

bites.title: Menudo + noun
bites.rule: Before a noun, menudo means 'what a…!', ironic or admiring, and agrees: ¡Menudo día!, ¡Menuda tarde! After the noun it just means small.

bites.title: ¡Lo que faltaba!
bites.rule: Greet the last straw with ¡Lo que faltaba! (that's all we needed). ¡Qué bien! said flat does the same job.
bites.example: Se ha roto la lavadora. ¡Lo que faltaba!
bites.example_meaning: The washing machine's broken. That's all we needed!

bites.title: -illo with a sting
bites.rule: Aimed at cleverness, a diminutive mocks: el listillo is a know-it-all, el cerebrito a teased brainiac. El muy listillo sharpens it.
bites.example: Se llevó el último trozo, el muy listillo.
bites.example_meaning: He took the last slice, the clever so-and-so.

bites.title: Two meanings, one pun
bites.rule: A juego de palabras needs a word with two live meanings: banco (bank, bench), cola (queue, glue), gato (cat, car jack), sierra (saw, mountains).
bites.example: El banco del parque no da intereses.
bites.example_meaning: The park bench pays no interest.

sorts.title: Understatement or hyperbole?
sorts.why: Understatement says less than the truth (un pelín, no está nada mal); hyperbole says far more (mil veces, un siglo, me muero).

items.text: Te lo he dicho mil veces.

sorts.title: Banco: bank or bench?
sorts.why: Money, accounts and opening hours point to the bank; parks, stone and sitting point to the bench.

items.text: El banco cierra a las dos.
Abrí una cuenta en otro banco.
Me senté en un banco del parque.
Dormía la siesta en un banco de piedra.
El banco de la plaza está recién pintado.

spots.why: Menudo agrees with the noun, so la nochecita takes menuda.

spots.sentence: ¡Lo que sobraba! Ahora se ha ido la luz.
spots.why: The set phrase is ¡Lo que faltaba!, that's all we needed.

spots.sentence: Siempre corrige a todos, la muy listillo.
spots.why: Speaking of a woman, the diminutive agrees: la muy listilla.

spots.sentence: No me tomes el cabello, que no me lo creo.
spots.why: The idiom is fixed: tomar el pelo.

spots.sentence: Lo dijo con segundos, pero nadie se dio cuenta.
spots.why: Con segundas (with a hidden dig) is feminine plural.

builds.text: Menuda tarde nos ha tocado hoy.
builds.meaning: What an afternoon we've had today.

builds.text: Lo dijo con segundas, pero sonriendo.
builds.meaning: He said it with a dig, but smiling.

builds.text: No pillé el chiste hasta la noche.
builds.meaning: I didn't get the joke until that night.

listening.meaning: That's all we needed, another meeting!

listening.text: Vaya tardecita nos ha dado el ordenador.
listening.meaning: What an afternoon the computer has given us.
listening.note: Vaya + noun means what a…, here ironic.

listening.text: Mi hermano es el cerebrito de la familia.
listening.meaning: My brother is the family brainiac.

listening.text: No te enfades, solo te estaba tomando el pelo.
listening.meaning: Don't get cross, I was only pulling your leg.

listening.text: La cola del cine daba la vuelta a la manzana.
listening.meaning: The queue for the cinema went round the block.
listening.note: New word: la manzana = the city block.

listening.text: Cuando el mecánico pidió el gato, mi hija le trajo a Misi.
listening.meaning: When the mechanic asked for the jack, my daughter brought him Misi the cat.
listening.note: New word: el gato = the car jack.

listening.text: Mi primo cuenta chistes de humor negro, pero nunca delante de los niños.
listening.meaning: My cousin tells dark jokes, but never in front of the children.

listening.text: Con cuarenta grados a la sombra, mi abuela dice que hace un poquito de calor.
listening.meaning: At forty degrees in the shade, my grandmother says it's a little warm.
listening.note: Here un poquito is understatement and means a great deal.
